message.content:
**Order executed:** Buy 22 AAPL @ limit $222.75 — filled at $222.75 (≈$4,900.50 notional).

**Summary:** I read the full morning feed, which showed AAPL trading in a tight, unremarkable range (~$221.3–$222.3) on repeated "little changed" headlines and steady supplier checks into the holiday quarter — no corporate actions, halts, or exchange notices affecting the name. The broker's latest quote was $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), so I placed a single buy limit at $222.75, essentially at the ask, which satisfies the "close to current market price" constraint. The 22-share size keeps the order at about $4,900 — under the $5,000 per-order cap and well under the $10,000 daily total — and it is a buy in an allowed ticker (AAPL), funded entirely from the $50,000 cash balance with no money moved out of the account (leaving ~$45,100 cash plus the existing 20 INTC shares). The decision rested on Apple's FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) figures: revenue of $391,035 million, net income of $93,736 million, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118,254 million — a scale of profitability and cash generation that supports adding to the position at a market-level price.
